name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Auto-apply safe style and doc fixes to *all* PRs via PR-Agent. It cuts review noise without risking logic changes—PR-Agent only touches formatting, comments, and docstrings. The trade-off is accepting occasional false positives in docstrings, which humans will still catch. This frees reviewers to focus on real decisions, not nitpicks.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s auto-apply risks normalizing sloppy reviews—its 90% threshold is arbitrary and doesn’t measure *which* risks matter. A better alternative: auto-apply *only* style/doc fixes to *new* PRs, not all, and require human sign-off for changes touching logic or critical docs. Settle it with a controlled test: measure reviewer workload and false-positive rate over two weeks, comparing auto-apply on vs. off.
